text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs wound up two days of talks in Bonn yesterday, saying Germany supports Hungary's need to join the EU and NATO at the earliest possible date.
- Parliament began debate on a proposal amending the 1992 law on compensation for those illegally deprived of their life and freedom for political reasons.

- Gyula Kosa, president of the Agricultural Producers Interest Protection Organisation, confirmed Tuesday that farmers are prepared to clash with police in order to impose a full blockade on roads leading to the capital and border crossings.

- The social democratic and left-wing leaders within the Socialist Party will meet on Friday evening and seek to hammer out a joint stance in favour of separating the posts of prime minister and party president.
- Culture and Education Minister Balint Magyar agreed yesterday with the heads of higher educational institutions on the payment of public servants' salaries.

- President Boris Yeltsin Tuesday vetoed a bill that declared all art treasures taken to Russia by Soviet troops in World War II to be Russian property. A list of 60,000 art objects missing from Hungary has been compiled.
- Welfare Minister Mihaly Kokeny yesterday urged a review of laws sanctioning the possession of drugs.
NEPSZABADSAG

- Constitutional Court president Laszlo Solyom Tuesday urged Parliament to fill the empty Court seat on the strength of existing constitutional regulations, rather than anticipate a new Constitution or constitutional amendment.
- At its weekly meeting tomorrow the cabinet is expected to discuss an amendment to the Penal Code.
- New Hungarian-US extradition and mutual legal aid agreements have taken effect after the ratification documents were exchanged in Washington yesterday.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Justice Minister Pal Vastagh said yesterday the cabinet expects to present to Parliament its constitutional amendment proposals in one package in April.
- The annual average yield of one-month treasury bills fell by 0.55 percent to 20.49 percent at yesterday's auction.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The January construction output came to HUF 20 billion, 6.5 percent more than in the same period last year.
- Yesterday's general meeting of the Hungarian Electricity Works approved plans to construct gas-powered back-up power plants near Sajoszoged and Liter.
- According to preliminary figures, Merkantil Bank Rt. realised a HUF 107.5 million pre-tax profit last year, up from HUF 67.1 million in 1995.
- Inter-Europa Bank board of directors plans to raise the company's equity from the present HUF 2.8 billion to HUF 7 billion by the end of the year.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The engine factory Audi Hungary Kft., based in Gyor, recorded an after-tax profit of DM 42.3 million last year on revenues of DM 622 million.

- This paper reports that Citibank and Daewoo are planning to bid on Konzumbank Rt., though its information is unconfirmed. Andras Huszty, managing director of the Hungarian Development Bank, which owns most of Konzumbank, said a sale of the bank was not planned but in case of a favourable offer it may be sold.
